findings.text: 61% of consumers believe bundles combining products with services or warranties create stronger value.

findings.text: 54% of consumers say they are making fewer impulse purchases, down from 71% the previous year.
findings.evidence: The report states: “54% say they are making fewer impulse purchases, down from 71% last year.”

findings.text: 52% of consumers use virtual assistants that automate reordering or meal planning at least once a week.
findings.evidence: The report states: “Almost half of consumers (52%) use virtual assistants that automate re-ordering or meal planning at least once a week.”

findings.text: 76% of consumers want the ability to set clear rules for when a virtual assistant acts.
findings.evidence: The executive summary states: “Seventy six percent want the ability to set clear rules for when an assistant acts.”

findings.text: 71% of consumers are worried about how generative AI uses their information.
findings.evidence: The report states that 71% are worried about lack of clarity on consent and transparency around collection and use of personal data.

findings.text: 74% of consumers said human interaction during in-store customer support increases loyalty in October 2025, compared with 54% in November 2024.
findings.evidence: Figure 23 reports customer-support figures of 54% for November 2024 and 74% for October 2025 for consumers who said human interaction increases loyalty.
findings.section_title: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries

findings.text: 66% of consumers said human interaction during the in-store purchase stage increases loyalty in October 2025, compared with 40% in November 2024.
findings.evidence: Figure 23 reports purchase-stage figures of 40% for November 2024 and 66% for October 2025 for consumers who said human interaction increases loyalty.
findings.section_title: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries

findings.text: 75% of consumers said money-off promotions are effective in driving purchase decisions.
findings.evidence: Figure 9 reports “Money-off (e.g., $5 off $25)” at 75% in response to how effective promotion types are in driving purchase decisions.

findings.text: 49% of consumers report looking to buy smaller quantities as prices rise.
findings.evidence: The report states: “around half (49%) are buying smaller quantities.”

findings.text: 48% of consumers report buying cheaper alternatives, such as canned fruit instead of fresh fruit, as prices rise.
findings.evidence: The report states: “A similar proportion (48%) are embracing cheaper alternatives, such as canned fruit instead of fresh.”

findings.text: Seven in ten consumers say small treats help them deal with financial stress.
findings.evidence: The report states: “Seven in ten shoppers in our survey say small treats help them deal with financial stress.”

findings.text: Among consumers, 11% are open to a one-time payment for chatbots or virtual shopping assistants, and 8% prefer a subscription model.
findings.evidence: Figure 14 reports 11% willing to pay as a one-time payment and 8% willing to pay for a monthly subscription.

findings.text: 63% of consumers want generative AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product or service recommendations based on their preferences.
findings.evidence: Figure 20 reports 63% agreeing: “I want Gen AI to provide hyper-personalized content and product/service recommendations based on my individual preferences.”
findings.section_title: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries

findings.text: Around two in five are choosing lower-cost alternatives, private labels, or smaller quantities to manage budgets, while nearly four in five avoid private labels in performance-critical categories.
findings.evidence: Around two in five are choosing lower cost alternatives, opting for private label, or buying smaller quantities to manage budgets. ... Nearly four in five avoid private labels in performance critical categories.

findings.text: Many have adopted a hybrid mindset, trading down in some categories while retaining spending in others, including when prioritizing health-related aspects.
findings.evidence: Many have adopted a hybrid mindset: willing to trade down in certain categories, while retaining spending in others (e.g., when prioritizing health-related aspects).
